Kitchen Renovation Cost DIY: UK Savings Guide

7 August 2026·BMB Renovation

Searching for kitchen renovation cost DIY figures usually means you want to improve the room without paying for every part of the work. That can be realistic, but the biggest savings often come from choosing the right tasks rather than attempting everything yourself. Painting, handles, shelving and some flat-pack assembly can be manageable for a careful homeowner. Electrical work, gas appliances, significant plumbing changes and poorly fitted cabinets can create safety, compliance and costly remedial problems. This guide explains where DIY may make sense in the UK, what professional help may cost and how to plan a mixed approach.

What does a DIY kitchen renovation cost in the UK?

As a rough guide, a modest DIY-led kitchen refresh might cost around £2,000 to £8,000, excluding major structural changes. That could cover paint, flooring, worktops, handles, a sink, taps, appliances and ready-to-assemble units, depending on the size and specification. A more substantial renovation using a mix of DIY and professional trades may typically fall around £8,000 to £18,000 or more. A fully fitted kitchen with higher-specification cabinets, new appliances, rewiring, replumbing or building work can exceed that range. These are broad UK estimates only: room size, product quality, access, location and the condition of the existing kitchen all affect the final price. Every project differs, so obtain a free quote for accurate pricing.

Where the potential saving comes from

  • Painting walls and ceilings: as a rough guide, materials may cost around £80–£250, while professional preparation and painting may cost several hundred pounds or more. The saving depends heavily on whether walls need filling, sanding or plaster repairs.
  • Removing old cabinets and appliances: DIY may save roughly £300–£1,000 in labour, but you remain responsible for safe disconnection, waste disposal and avoiding damage to walls, flooring and services.
  • Flat-pack cabinet assembly: a careful homeowner may save roughly £500–£1,500 on a small or medium kitchen. The real challenge is achieving level, square units and accurate spacing for doors, drawers and worktops.
  • Handles, shelves and simple splashback panels: as a rough guide, materials might range from £50–£600, with a possible labour saving of around £100–£500. Measure carefully before drilling into walls or doors.
  • Laminate flooring: a straightforward room may typically cost around £200–£800 in materials. Professional installation may add several hundred pounds, particularly if the subfloor needs levelling or existing flooring must be removed.

Kitchen renovation tasks that are usually suitable for DIY

DIY is most sensible when a mistake is inconvenient rather than dangerous or expensive to correct. Decorating is a good example: remove fittings, protect worktops, prepare the surfaces properly and apply several thin coats rather than rushing one thick coat. Replacing handles, fitting open shelves and installing simple trim can also be achievable with basic tools. If you are changing flooring, check that the surface is dry, clean and sufficiently level, and follow the manufacturer's guidance around expansion gaps and adhesive. A kitchen renovation can often look fresher without moving the sink, cooker or walls.

You may also be able to assemble cabinets yourself, but installation is a different skill from assembly. Units need to be fixed securely, aligned across the room and accurately scribed to uneven walls. Worktop cutting, especially around a sink or hob, requires precision and suitable equipment. If the kitchen layout is staying the same and you are confident with measuring, assembly can reduce the bill; if the layout is changing, professional installation may be better value than correcting a row of misaligned units.

When professional help is essential

  • Electrical alterations: adding sockets, moving circuits, installing lighting or changing the supply for an oven or induction hob should be planned and completed safely. Depending on the work and location, building regulations requirements and notification may apply; use a competent electrician where appropriate.
  • Gas work: connecting, moving or disconnecting a gas hob or cooker should be handled by a Gas Safe registered engineer. Do not treat this as a DIY saving.
  • Plumbing changes: moving a sink, dishwasher or washing machine can involve new pipework, waste falls, isolation valves and leak testing. A small hidden leak can cause serious damage to cabinets and flooring.
  • Structural alterations: removing walls, widening openings or changing windows may require structural design, planning permission or building control input. Do not assume a wall is non-load-bearing because it looks lightweight.
  • Cabinet and worktop installation: professional fitting can be particularly valuable with uneven walls, bespoke units, heavy stone worktops, integrated appliances or a layout that differs from the old kitchen.
  • Floor and wall preparation: severe damp, failed plaster, uneven floors or damaged subfloors should be diagnosed before new finishes are installed. Covering the problem usually postpones rather than removes the cost.

The cost of hiring professionals for selected work

Rather than choosing between a completely DIY renovation and a full-service project, many homeowners use a hybrid plan. As rough guides, decorating may cost from several hundred pounds, cabinet installation may typically add around £1,000–£3,000 depending on the kitchen, and flooring installation may add roughly £300–£1,200. Plumbing alterations, electrical work and appliance connections are priced according to the number of points, the distance services must move and whether the existing installation needs upgrading. Worktop fitting can range from a few hundred pounds for straightforward laminate to considerably more for templated stone or specialist materials. Every project is different, so get a free quote for accurate pricing and ensure written quotations state exactly what is included, including removal, waste, preparation, finishing and connections.

How to keep a DIY kitchen renovation on budget

  • Keep the existing layout where possible. Moving water, waste, gas and electrical points can add to the cost of a renovation.
  • Create a measured plan before ordering. Include appliance dimensions, door clearances, service voids, worktop overhangs and filler panels.
  • Budget for preparation, delivery, waste removal, fixings, sealants, trims and replacement parts. These smaller items can be missed in a product-only estimate.
  • Do not buy cabinets before checking wall lengths, floor levels and appliance compatibility. A return or replacement can remove any DIY saving.
  • Agree the division of work with tradespeople in advance. For example, you might remove loose finishes and paint while the installer completes plumbing, electrical work, cabinets and worktops.
  • Consider a contingency allowance for unexpected repairs or changes; as a rough planning guide, some homeowners allow around 10–15%, but the appropriate amount depends on the project.

The safest way to estimate kitchen renovation cost DIY is to price three versions: a DIY refresh, a hybrid renovation and a professionally managed installation. Compare like for like, including materials, labour, waste, preparation and the cost of correcting mistakes. If your plans involve only cosmetic changes, DIY may deliver a worthwhile saving. If the project changes services, appliances, structure or the kitchen layout, using the relevant professional help may be the more predictable option.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much can I save by fitting a kitchen myself?+
As a rough guide, DIY cabinet assembly, decorating and simple finishing work might save several hundred to a few thousand pounds. The saving depends on the kitchen size, your skill, tools and whether professional work is still needed for services and worktops. Every project differs, so get a free quote for accurate pricing.
Can I install my own kitchen cabinets?+
You can assemble and sometimes install cabinets yourself if you are confident with measuring, levelling and fixing. Professional fitting can be useful for uneven rooms, complex layouts, integrated appliances, heavy worktops or cabinets requiring accurate scribing.
What kitchen renovation work must not be DIY?+
Gas work should be completed by a Gas Safe registered engineer. Electrical alterations, significant plumbing changes and structural work should be planned carefully and may require competent professionals, building regulations compliance or other approvals depending on the work.
Is it cheaper to renovate a kitchen or replace it?+
A refresh may cost less if the cabinets, layout and services are in good condition. Replacing doors, handles, worktops, flooring or paint can cost less than a full refit, while a new kitchen may be more suitable when units are damaged or the layout no longer works.
Should I use a professional for a DIY kitchen renovation in the UK?+
A hybrid approach can be practical: complete decorating and simple finishing tasks yourself, then use appropriate professionals for gas work and, where needed, electrical, plumbing, structural, cabinet and worktop work. Get a detailed quote so the responsibilities and costs are clear.
